base_rationale: GG (Gunda Gundē GG-00106) is recommended as the base witness on the evidence: (1) completeness — GG transcribes all 28 verses with only its col-3 right-edge water stain causing 15 localized lacunae confined to vv.21-28, whereas CAM's low-res crop yields 176 uncertain tokens (~44%) spread across every verse; (2) lower base uncertainty — GG's uncertainty is 21.9% vs CAM's 44.0%, and GG's is clustered (damage + proper names) rather than pervasive; (3) clearer hand at ~5MP vs CAM's ~0.6MP, so cols 1-2 (vv.1-20) are a genuine letter-by-letter read; (4) the skeleton-level agreements more often confirm GG's fuller text. NOTE / CONTRADICTION: the GAPS source-map a-priori designates Cambridge Add. 1570 the "primary" witness for Samuel and GG-00106 the "second witness"; this empirical calibration INVERTS that for 1 Samuel 1 — at the resolutions actually supplied, GG is materially the stronger base. This contradiction is surfaced, not hidden; the a-priori map ranking should be revisited for Samuel or Cambridge re-shot at higher resolution before it can serve as base.

metrics.asymmetry_note: Image-resolution asymmetry is severe: GG-00106 ≈ 5 MP full-page scans vs Cambridge Add. 1570 ≈ 0.6 MP crop (~0.5-0.6 MP effective for this chapter). The STRICT number is confounded — it largely measures CAM's vowel-order diacritic illegibility (image quality), not scribal variance. The SKELETON and BOTH-CONFIDENT figures are the honest reads: skeleton isolates true word-choice variance by collapsing the 7 vowel orders + folding near-homographs (ሰ/ሠ, ሐ/ኀ/ሀ, አ/ዐ, ጸ/ፀ, ጠ/ጰ); both-confident further restricts to tokens neither scribe flagged. GG's lacunae are damage-clustered (col-3 stain, vv.21-28); CAM's uncertainty is pervasive and resolution-driven.
